key_claims: The 'wheel of jihad': Pakistan stood up the Afghan Taliban, which is in bed with al-Qaeda, which stood up the TTP, which attacks the Pakistani state - and Pakistan keeps supporting the Afghan Taliban anyway.

The 'good Taliban / bad Taliban' distinction was always phony; TTP and Afghan Taliban share personnel, training, leadership, funding and ideology, and the UN now documents Taliban support for ~6,000 TTP fighters.
The Doha agreement pledge that no terrorists would operate from Afghan soil is exposed as a lie by Pakistan's need for a ceasefire with the Taliban.
Noor Wali Mehsud was targeted in Kabul, the same city where Zawahiri hid - Taliban sanctuary for senior terrorists is systematic.
TTP seeks a nuclear-armed Taliban-style emirate in Pakistan; its insurgency is at a pre-control 'prelude' stage, not yet at 2006-2013 peak.
Pakistan will likely not turn decisively on the Afghan Taliban because of strategic depth against India and sympathizers inside the military/ISI (Section S).
Al-Qaeda and ISIS share the caliphate end-state ('build the emirate' vs 'caliphate now'); AQIS under Osama Mahmood is a wild card for exporting jihad into India.
